anatomy.title: Anatomia
anatomy.item1: Table — wrapper <div> com overflow-x-auto e elemento <table> com caption-bottom text-sm.
anatomy.item2: TableHeader — elemento <thead> com borda inferior em todas as linhas internas.
anatomy.item3: TableBody — elemento <tbody> que agrupa as linhas de dados, sem borda na última linha.
anatomy.item4: TableFooter — elemento <tfoot> com fundo bg-muted/50 e tipografia em font-medium para destacar totais.
anatomy.item5: TableRow — elemento <tr> com borda inferior, hover bg-muted/50 e estado selecionado via data-state="selected".
anatomy.item6: TableHead — elemento <th> com altura 40px, alinhamento à esquerda e cor text-muted-foreground.
anatomy.item8: TableCaption — elemento <caption> renderizado abaixo da tabela (caption-bottom), com texto discreto.

guidelines.title: 📋 Guidelines Obrigatórias
guidelines.item1: Use <caption> para descrever o conteúdo da tabela — é anunciado por leitores de tela antes dos cabeçalhos.
guidelines.item2: Alinhe colunas numéricas à direita com text-right para facilitar a comparação de valores.
guidelines.item3: Envolva o wrapper em overflow-x-auto para evitar quebra de layout em viewports estreitos.
guidelines.item4: Use <tfoot> para totais e agregações — é semanticamente correto e visualmente destacado.

accessibility.title: Acessibilidade
accessibility.item1: Estrutura semântica — usa <table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot> nativos, que leitores de tela reconhecem automaticamente.
accessibility.item2: Caption — descreva a tabela em <caption>; é o primeiro elemento anunciado ao entrar na tabela.
accessibility.item3: Scope — use scope="col" em TableHead de colunas e scope="row" quando a primeira célula da linha for cabeçalho.
accessibility.item4: Alinhamento numérico — valores numéricos à direita (text-right) facilitam comparação visual e são esperados por usuários de planilhas.
accessibility.item5: Contraste — texto do cabeçalho (text-muted-foreground) mantém contraste ≥ 4.5:1 contra o fundo padrão.

keyboard.tab: Move o foco para a próxima célula interativa (link, botão, checkbox).
keyboard.arrows: Não há navegação por setas nativa — adicione manualmente se implementar seleção por teclado.
keyboard.enter: Ativa o elemento interativo focado dentro da célula.

notes.tip2: Em mobile, prefira reduzir o número de colunas ou transformar linhas em cards — a rolagem horizontal resolve casos simples, mas piora a UX em tabelas largas.

anatomy.title: Anatomy
anatomy.item1: Table — <div> wrapper with overflow-x-auto and a <table> element with caption-bottom text-sm.
anatomy.item2: TableHeader — <thead> element with bottom border on all inner rows.
anatomy.item3: TableBody — <tbody> element grouping data rows, with no border on the last row.
anatomy.item4: TableFooter — <tfoot> element with bg-muted/50 background and font-medium typography to highlight totals.
anatomy.item5: TableRow — <tr> element with bottom border, bg-muted/50 on hover, and selected state via data-state="selected".
anatomy.item6: TableHead — <th> element with 40px height, left alignment, and text-muted-foreground color.
anatomy.item8: TableCaption — <caption> element rendered below the table (caption-bottom), with subtle text.

guidelines.title: 📋 Mandatory Guidelines
guidelines.item1: Use <caption> to describe the table content — it's announced by screen readers before the headers.
guidelines.item2: Right-align numeric columns with text-right to ease comparison of values.
guidelines.item3: Wrap in overflow-x-auto to prevent layout breakage on narrow viewports.
guidelines.item4: Use <tfoot> for totals and aggregations — semantically correct and visually highlighted.

item4.s: Card list with image and title

do.title: Use when
do.item1: Data has row × column relationship and needs comparison
do.item2: Users need to read numeric values or dates side by side
do.item3: Sorting, filtering or row selection is part of the task
do.item4: The dataset fits without excessive vertical scroll (< 50 rows)

dont.title: Don't use when
dont.item1: The content is purely visual — prefer CSS Grid for layout
dont.item2: Each row is a rich entity with imagery — prefer Card Grid
dont.item3: These are editable fields of a single record — prefer Form

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.item1: Semantic structure — uses native <table>, <thead>, <tbody>, <tfoot>, automatically recognized by screen readers.
accessibility.item2: Caption — describe the table in <caption>; it's the first element announced when entering the table.
accessibility.item3: Scope — use scope="col" on column TableHead and scope="row" when the first cell of a row is a header.
accessibility.item4: Numeric alignment — right-align numeric values (text-right) for easier visual comparison and to match spreadsheet user expectations.
accessibility.item5: Contrast — header text (text-muted-foreground) maintains ≥ 4.5:1 contrast against the default background.

keyboard.tab: Moves focus to the next interactive cell (link, button, checkbox).
keyboard.arrows: No native arrow navigation — add manually if implementing keyboard selection.
keyboard.enter: Activates the focused interactive element inside the cell.

related.card: For lists of rich entities with image and title.
related.dataTable: For interactive tables with sort, filter and pagination.
related.pagination: To split long tables into pages.

notes.title: Notes and Tips
notes.tip1: For tables with more than 1000 rows, add virtualization (react-virtual, TanStack Table) to keep performance.
notes.tip2: On mobile, prefer reducing the number of columns or converting rows into cards — horizontal scroll solves simple cases but degrades UX on wide tables.
